specimen.purpose: Selected org alias, uppercase. Fitted to the largest of 48/40/32/24/16 CSS px that fits without wrapping; each step snapped to a whole multiple of 8 device pixels.

title.purpose: State headlines and secondary-view bitmap headlines (the hotkey is the Settings specimen). Token --fs-title, DPR-snapped.

keycap.purpose: Hotkey keycaps and the plus between them. Token --fs-cap, DPR-snapped.

code.purpose: Ribbons and env tags (700, 0.04em); footer keys, row serials, setting labels (400). Token --fs-code, DPR-snapped.

body.purpose: Sub line, descriptions, setting values, state paragraphs (max 46ch). Tabular numerals.

label.purpose: Button text (600); footer and usage counts (500).

pixelGrid.resnap: On matchMedia resolution change (monitor move, zoom).

glass.name: glass
glass.purpose: Default panel background in a transparent, frameless 620x520 window.

glass.name: no-glass
glass.purpose: Applied via :root.no-glass when Windows transparency effects are off, and under prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce.

glass.name: dot-screen
glass.value: radial-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0.6) 0.6px, transparent 0.8px) 4px grid, opacity 0.18, masked to fade by 38%
glass.purpose: Etched texture at the panel's top edge only.

shadows.name: toast-lift
shadows.purpose: The toast, the only floating element.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Panel entry (140ms, 6px drop) and toast entry (160ms).

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background/color transitions on buttons, rows, cards.

narrative.northStar: The Bitmap Specimen on Smoked Glass
narrative.overview:
One fixed 620×520 frameless window, always on top, floating over whatever the user was doing. The window is Windows 11 Acrylic; the panel tints it with VS Code Dark black so the desktop shows through as a dim blur. Inside, the selected org is set as a type specimen in a bitmap face, as large as its name allows, with a solid rule underneath in its environment colour. Everything else (the search bar, the identical list rows, the shortcut footer) is set small in a quiet grotesque and stays out of the way.

The system is dense and keyboard-first. Hierarchy comes from scale contrast between the pixel headline and everything else, not from colour or weight. Colour is semantic: one acid lime for focus and the primary action, one colour per Salesforce environment, and red for anything that touches production. The pixel face carries over into small codes (environment tags, keys, row serials, setting labels), the Enter glyph, the progress bar, and the tray icon, so the bitmap grid reads as the house material rather than a headline gimmick.
keyCharacteristics: Smoked glass panel (74% VS Code black over Acrylic) with a 1px light edge and a fading etched dot screen at the top.
Silkscreen bitmap for the specimen, titles, and every code or key; Hanken Grotesk for everything read.
Every bitmap size snapped to whole multiples of 8 device pixels, re-snapped on display-scale change.
Acid lime is reserved for focus, the primary action, and success; environment colours carry identity; production is red everywhere.
Motion is short and stepped where it touches the pixel world (reveal, skeleton scan); everything collapses under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Acid Rule
rules.body: Lime means "this is focused" or "this is the action". It never decorates and never labels an environment.

rules.name: The Production Is Red Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Production and Dev Hub share prod-red on every surface: ribbon, tag, specimen ink, selected-row ring. Dev Hubs live in production orgs and get the same warning; there is no separate Dev Hub colour.

rules.name: The Ribbon Per Environment Rule
rules.body: Each environment owns exactly one colour, used as ribbon fill, tag text and border, and specimen underline. Do not add a second hue for an environment or reuse an environment hue for anything else.

rules.name: The Pixel Grid Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen is only ever set at a size that is a whole multiple of 8 device pixels at the current devicePixelRatio. Sizes are declared as targets in CSS px and snapped at runtime (`round(target × dpr / 8) × 8 / dpr`), and re-snapped when the window moves to a display with a different scale. Never hard-code a bitmap font size in CSS without routing it through the snapper.

rules.name: The Bitmap Means Name Or Key Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen sets names, codes, and keys only. Sentences, usernames, descriptions, and button labels stay in Hanken Grotesk.

rules.name: The One Key Notation Rule
rules.body: Shortcuts are written `Ctrl L`, `Ctrl 1-9`, `Esc` (space-separated, no plus signs), and Enter is always the pixel Enter glyph, never the ↵ character.

rules.name: The Glass Or Solid Rule
rules.body: The panel is glass when Windows transparency is on and solid VS Code black when it is off or reduced transparency is requested. Never let the Acrylic fallback grey show.

rules.name: The Etched Screen Rule
rules.body: A 4px dot screen at 18% opacity fades out over the top 38% of the panel. It is the only texture; it never covers content density elsewhere.

dos: Do route every Silkscreen size through the pixel-grid snapper and pick from the 48/40/32/24/16 steps for fitted headlines.
Do colour an org by its environment only, and treat Dev Hub exactly like production.
Do keep the 18px gutter and identical 40px rows; selection changes tint and ring, never size.
Do fall back to solid VS Code black (#1E1E1E) whenever transparency is off or reduced.
Do write shortcuts as `Ctrl X` and draw Enter with the pixel glyph.
Do use stepped timing for pixel-world motion and honour reduced motion by removing all animation.
donts: Don't use acid lime for decoration, environment identity, or large fills beyond the primary button and success toast.
Don't set sentences, usernames, or button labels in Silkscreen.
Don't set Silkscreen at an unsnapped size; fractional device pixels blur the bitmap.
Don't round ribbons, env tags, progress cells, or the specimen rule.
Don't use the ↵ character or `Ctrl+` notation.
